Town hall on the river bridge, transcript prepared by the county clerk.

MODERATOR: Good evening. We are here to talk about the river bridge. Mayor, you first.

MAYOR HALE: Thank you. The bridge is sixty years old and the inspectors have
told us plainly that it needs work within five years. (APPLAUSE) We have a plan
to pay for it without raising the levy.

MAYOR HALE: The plan uses the state fund and the reserve we built up.

MODERATOR: Councillor, your answer.

COUNCILLOR (DISTRICT 2): That reserve was meant for the flood defences. [CROSSTALK]
If we spend it on the bridge we are one bad spring away from disaster.

MAYOR HALE: That is not true. (inaudible) The defences are funded separately.

COUNCILLOR (DISTRICT 2): Then show us the numbers. (LAUGHTER) Put them on the
table tonight and let people read them.

MODERATOR: We will take questions after a short break.
